nodes.title: the Opalopal signature
nodes.statement: The Opalopal system concerns objects called xilzams. There are exactly 4 of them: muxovi, nyrfex, ovimux, shennak. Two operations are written & and $. One relation is written <|, read as "yields to".

nodes.title: the Opalopal combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x & y for every pair of xilzams is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for $. The pairs standing in the <| relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x and y, x & y is again a xilzam.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x, y, z: (x & y) & z = x & (y & z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x and y: x & y = y & x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a xilzam muxovi with muxovi & x = x & muxovi = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a xilzam shennak with shennak & x = x & shennak = shennak for every x.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x and y, x $ y is again a xilzam.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x, y, z: (x $ y) $ z = x $ (y $ z).

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every xilzam x: x $ x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every xilzam x: x <| x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x and y: if x <| y and y <| x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x, y, z: if x <| y and y <| z then x <| z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x and y, at least one of x <| y and y <| x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x, y, z: if x <| y then (z & x) <| (z & y) and (x & z) <| (y & z).

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all xilzams x, y, z: if x <| y then (z $ x) <| (z $ y) and (x $ z) <| (y $ z).

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some xilzam x admits no xilzam y for which x & y and y & x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nyrfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every xilzam x: x & x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nyrfex, value = ovimux, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all xilzams x, y, z: if x & y = x & z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nyrfex, y = ovimux, z = shennak, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all xilzams x and y: x $ y = y $ x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = muxovi, y = nyrfex, left = nyrfex, right = muxovi, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is no xilzam that leaves every xilzam unchanged under the second operation.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case reason = no two sided identity exists, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have spreading of the second operation over the first
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all xilzams x, y, z: x $ (y & z) = (x $ y) & (x $ z), and the same on the right.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nyrfex, y = muxovi, z = muxovi, left = nyrfex, right = ovimux, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have the absorption pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all xilzams x and y: x & (x $ y) = x and x $ (x & y) = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = muxovi, y = nyrfex, value = nyrfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: thrami xilzams
nodes.statement: A xilzam x is called thrami when x & x = x.

nodes.title: xilzams that reldjen
nodes.statement: Two xilzams x and y are said to reldjen when x & y = y & x.

nodes.title: hurnkeld collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of xilzams is hurnkeld when x & y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the mivint of a xilzam
nodes.statement: The mivint of a xilzam x is the collection of xilzams y for which x <| y holds.

nodes.title: the minak
nodes.statement: The xilzam muxovi is called the minak of the system. It is the unique xilzam that leaves every xilzam unchanged under &.

nodes.title: the sibnak
nodes.statement: The sibnak of the system is the collection of xilzams that reldjen with every xilzam.

nodes.title: the mornmi
nodes.statement: The mornmi is the collection of all thrami xilzams.

nodes.title: the ponwren of a xilzam
nodes.statement: The ponwren of a xilzam x, written [x], is the smallest hurnkeld collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a umbmux
nodes.statement: A xilzam f is a umbmux when f <| y holds for every xilzam y, that is, when the mivint of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: tuvor xilzams
nodes.statement: A xilzam x is tuvor when x & x equals the minak.

nodes.title: the falisk of a xilzam
nodes.statement: The falisk of a xilzam x is the number of xilzams in its ponwren [x].

nodes.title: the vashquil
nodes.statement: The vashquil of the system is the collection of xilzams whose falisk is largest.

nodes.title: duthtu pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct xilzams x and y form a duthtu pair when x <| y and y <| x both hold, that is, when each lies in the mivint of the other.

nodes.title: the minak is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one xilzam e with e & x = x & e = x for every xilzam x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every xilzam unchanged.
Then e & f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e & f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the minak lies in the sibnak
nodes.statement: The minak reldjens with every xilzam.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the minak and x any xilzam.
Then e & x = x and x & e = x.
So e & x = x & e, which is what it means to reldjen.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the sibnak.

nodes.title: the sibnak is hurnkeld
nodes.statement: If x and y both reldjen with every xilzam, then so does x & y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the sibnak and let z be any xilzam.
Then (x & y) & z = x & (y & z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each reldjens with everything.
So x & y reldjens with z, and the sibnak is hurnkeld.

nodes.title: the ponwren of a xilzam is hurnkeld
nodes.statement: For every xilzam x, the collection [x] is hurnkeld.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under &.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the ponwren is contained in every hurnkeld collection
nodes.statement: If S is hurnkeld and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a xilzam is thrami exactly when its falisk is one
nodes.statement: x & x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x & x = x then {x} is already closed under &.
So [x] = {x} and the falisk is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x & x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the falisk divides the number of xilzams breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every xilzam x, the falisk of x divides 4.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nyrfex, reach = 3, size = 4, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the ponwren of a sibnak xilzam stays in the sibnak
nodes.statement: If x lies in the sibnak then every xilzam of [x] lies in the sibnak.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The sibnak is hurnkeld.
[x] is the smallest hurnkeld collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the sibnak is one.

nodes.title: the mornmi is hurnkeld
nodes.statement: If x and y are both thrami then so is x & y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be thrami.
The claim asks whether (x & y) & (x & y) returns x & y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: mivints are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the mivint of x, then the mivint of y is contained in the mivint of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x <| y and let z satisfy y <| z.
Transitivity gives x <| z.
So every member of the mivint of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one umbmux
nodes.statement: No two distinct xilzams can both be umbmuxs.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f <| h, since h is any object, and h <| f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a umbmux
nodes.statement: Some xilzam umbmuxs the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x <| y then (x & z) <| (y & z) for every xilzam z.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the mivint of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: no duthtu pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct xilzams lie in each other's mivint.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every xilzam lies in the sibnak
nodes.statement: Every pair of xilzams reldjens.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The sibnak is defined by reldjening with everything.
The claim is that x & y = y & x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every xilzam is thrami breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x & x = x for every xilzam x.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nyrfex, value = ovimux, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where some xilzam reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a xilzam whose ponwren is the whole system.

verification.domain: every object and its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case largest_span = 3, size = 4, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x <| y then y <| x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = muxovi, y = nyrfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the minak swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e & x equals the minak for every xilzam x.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = muxovi, x = nyrfex, value = nyrfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the sibnak intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the sibnak then so does x $ y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The sibnak is already hurnkeld under &.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that $ respects the sibnak as well.
